body.p: Claims 1-4 and 6-13 have been rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102 by Anderson (US 2012/0083947).
Independent claims 1 and 9 have been amended to more clearly recite that
which the applicant regards as being patentable. Many of the dependent claims have been amended for consistency.
The claims address the problem of a vehicle and it occupants from being

threatened in the situation where attackers use another vehicle in front of the vehicle to force the vehicle to slow. An attacker on foot may then approach the vehicle. This scenario has unfortunately become a common ploy by criminals and can lead to serious injury of the vehicle's occupants.
Sometimes the situation can be avoided if an astute driver recognizes the situation and takes immediate action. But the driver and other occupants may not always be so lucky.

As autonomous driving becomes more of a possibility, attackers may take advantage of the fact the occupants may not pay as much attention to their surroundings-or even have the ability to control the vehicle. Thus, these types of attacks may be even easier to perpetrate against autonomous vehicles.
As such, there is a need for technology to detect these attacks and take
mitigating action. This is something that the prior art does not teach or reasonably suggest.
For example, Anderson is directed to a collision avoidance system in a vehicle.

While Anderson may make determinations about surroundings of the vehicle, it does not disclose making a threat assessment based on another vehicle slowing down in an absence of a traffic related reason to slow down and a person approaching the vehicle.
In view of the teaching deficiencies of Anderson, withdrawal of the rejections under 35 U.S.C. § 102 is respectfully requested.
Claim 5 has been rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 over Anderson in view of Visintainer (US 2021/0118295).

Visintainer, like Anderson, is directed to a driver assistance system. While Visintainer might track behavior of vehicles in adjacent lanes, Visintainer does not detect the threat posed in the claims. Nor does Visintainer make any determinations that would detect a threatening action resulting from a "box-in" maneuver employed by attackers using two vehicles.
Therefore, Visintainer does not cure the teaching deficiencies of Anderson and
even if the proposed combination were attempted, the claimed subject matter would not result. Accordingly, withdrawal of the rejections under 35 U.S.C. § 103 is respectfully requested.
